> A tabletop robot that teaches a parent and child a language together, instead of instructing the child alone. Many caregivers get left behind when a child's language learning happens outside the home, so Tandem keeps the parent an active learner and participant throughout. A camera and microphone let it notice what's happening in front of it, such as a snack, a toy or a picture book. It uses that to anchor vocabulary and dialogue to the activity, so the target language stays relevant to both of them. The hardware is a friendly screen-faced body with a camera "eye", a speaker, a tap-to-talk button and expressive arms that point and wave at things. What makes it mine is that I'm designing the body around the interaction, so the camera, mic and speaker are placed for a shared moment between two people rather than hidden in a generic box.
